answer: The trellis multiplier is published, charged in falcon, and juniper lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4960 identities would post 1117 proofs and burn roughly 58 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
